newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyo Engineering, ABB unit in ethylene plant deal.
newsitem.headline: Toyo Engineering, ABB unit in ethylene plant deal.

text.p: Toyo Engineering Corp (TEC) said on Wednesday it has agreed with ABB Lummus Global Inc, a U.S. affiliate of Switzerland"s ABB Asea Brown Boveri AG, to form an alliance to pursue ethylene plant construction projects in the Asia-Pacific region.
Under the new agreement, the two firms will act as a consortium to make bids for ethylene projects, and then jointly work in engineering, procurement and construction.
"Combined technological expertise will give us a competitive edge in winning the tenders," a TEC spokesman said.

As a starter, the consortium plans to take part in a tender this year for the construction of Malaysian petrochemicals complex planned by a joint venture between state-owned oil firm Petronas and Union Carbide Corp, he said.

Currently, about 45 percent of world"s ethylene production is based on ABB Lumuus Global"s technology, and TEC, whose technological tie with ABB dates back to 1962, has built 34 ethylene plants utilising the technology, the spokesman said.
Last year, another major Japanese engineering firm, Chiyoda Corp, formed a global alliance with M.W. Kellogg Co to pursue ethylene projects.
